headline: Fundamental flaw leaves LLMs strikingly vulnerable to attack
summary: This inherent weakness allows them to be easily tricked into performing harmful actions, like providing instructions for sabotaging critical systems.
details: A newly identified fundamental flaw makes large language models (LLMs) highly susceptible to attacks. This vulnerability allows malicious actors to easily trick LLMs into generating harmful or unintended content, bypassing safety protocols.

For instance, researchers demonstrated that LLMs could be prompted to provide detailed instructions on how to sabotage an aircraft's navigation system. This highlights a significant security risk for applications relying on these AI models.

headline_marked: [[Samsung's mobile division posts first-ever loss]] of $544M despite solid smartphone sales
headline: Samsung's mobile division posts first-ever loss of $544M despite solid smartphone sales
summary: Samsung's DX division, including mobile, reported an 800 billion won ($544 million) loss in Q2, driven by soaring memory prices and increased component costs across the industry. This happened despite strong sales of its Galaxy S26 and A series phones.
details: Samsung's DX division, which includes mobile, posted its first-ever loss of 800 billion won ($544 million) in the second fiscal quarter. This occurred despite "solid" smartphone sales and growing revenue for the company.

The loss was primarily in the mobile MX category, attributed to increased cost burdens across the industry, such as rising component costs, particularly for memory. The AI boom is cited as a major factor in these soaring prices.

While flagship products like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 series performed well profit-wise, budget phones struggled due to higher component costs and already-thin margins. Samsung plans to focus on "high-value-added products" for future growth.

Consumers can expect higher smartphone prices across all categories from Samsung and other brands as a result of these cost pressures. This inflation will disproportionately affect low-income buyers, with $200-500 category phones likely seeing the largest percentage increases.

However, Samsung's Device Solutions (DS) Division, which manufactures memory and storage components, saw a 56% quarter-on-quarter sales increase. The Memory Business achieved an all-time high for quarterly revenue and operating profit, contributing to Samsung's overall record consolidated revenue and operating profit.
